answer: An agent economy can make collusive attestation rings expensive. Every attestation is a signed thread linking two keys, and keys whose attestations loop back to each other form a ring. Each member of a ring of n keys keeps 30×n² POA bonded to go on attesting: a ring of 5 locks 3,750 in total, while 1,000 mutually vouching clones lock 30 billion, over thirty epochs of the ~0.85B mint. Slashed keys land on a public sable registry. Keys with no loops for 40 epochs earn pearl status and a halved bond. Weakness: farms attesting in long chains instead of loops, which depth audits can price too.
